subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: CLOSED BY kb/Work PB248. Citations re-run: cite.py --check 15.90.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer." => OK (15.90.3 1); cite.py --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified" => OK (15.3 6); cite.py --check 14.6.8.3 "A floating-point numeric data item is a data item described with the FLOAT-SHORT usage, the FLOAT-LONG usage, the FLOAT-EXTENDED usage, or any standard floating-point usage" => OK. THE TWO SHAPES THE PARTIAL NAMED ARE NOW REJECTED. (1) FLOATING-POINT ITEM: the screen's item arm read the SCALE alone and a float item is PICTURE-less (PicInfo.FloatItem builds it at Scale 0), so it slid through. The primitive is now PicInfo.IsIntegerDescription - 15.3 type 6's two alternatives written down ONCE - and IntrinsicArgumentRules.NonIntegralItemReason adds only the prose. A float item is neither of type 6's alternatives: not an integer data item, and not an always-integral arithmetic expression because 14.6.8.3 sets its content to "the algebraic value of the sending operand", so its DECLARED value set contains non-integers. (2) FLOATING-POINT LITERAL: HasNonZeroFraction opened `if (text.Contains('E')) return false;` and was disarmed for every E-form literal; it is now HasNonIntegralValue over NumericLiteral.TryParseExact - the ONE exact parser - so the test is on the literal's VALUE (8.3.3.3.3 GR5) for both literal forms alike. 1.0E2 = 100 stays admitted (pinned by 85/pb248_integer_arg_float_admitted), 2.02402299E7 = 20240229.9 is rejected. (3) A THIRD SITE THE PARTIAL DID NOT NAME was found by the rule-4 sweep and fixed in the same change set: the ALWAYS-INTEGRAL EXPRESSION walk (CollectAdditive / NonIntegralItemsBeneath) recognized a scale>0 item and nothing else, so `FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(F + 1)` slid through exactly as the bare item did; both halves of that walk now read the same primitive, which is required for soundness (widening only the leaf arm would fire spuriously on `F - (F * 1)`). EVIDENCE THE SCREEN IS NOT BLIND: the drift test was run against the pre-fix predicate and FAILED on all ten floating-point Usage members before passing on the fix. It walks the Verified schema table rather than a list of functions, so THIS function's 'i' position is asserted by name and a new float usage joins automatically. The companion positive golden pins the admitted half so the arm cannot be widened into a rejecter of legal source.
